questions.q: Why is a code rollback mechanically simple compared to a data rollback?
options: Lessons 45-46 already built the machinery for reverting and redeploying — but the bad code has already run and already written real rows and shown real numbers before the rollback happens
Code rollbacks and data rollbacks are actually the same operation
Data rollbacks are always simpler and faster than code rollbacks
Neither type of rollback is ever actually possible
questions.explain: Reverting the code stops the bleeding going forward, but does nothing about what already happened.

questions.q: What makes Delta's time travel (Databricks Lesson 21) the closest thing to a real data rollback?
options: It can restore a Delta table to a version before a bad write happened, but only within its retention window and only for applicable tables
It can undo any data change instantly, with no limitations
It works identically for KQL Databases and Delta tables
Time travel has nothing to do with data rollback at all
questions.explain: A KQL Database has no equivalent built-in mechanism — undoing bad streamed data there usually means a manual, targeted correction.

questions.q: What kind of side effect can a rollback never undo, even in principle?
options: An Activator alert that already notified a real person, or a decision a dispatcher already made based on a wrong number
A KQL query that hasn't run yet
A Fabric Capacity SKU that hasn't been changed
A dev/test environment that was never actually deployed to
questions.explain: This is exactly why mitigation (Lesson 57) matters as its own step — some damage is only preventable, not fixable afterward.

questions.q: When might a forward fix be a better choice than a full rollback?
options: If the previous version had its own known issues, or the bug is small and well-understood, a targeted forward fix through CI/CD can resolve things faster
A forward fix is never actually a valid alternative to rollback
Rollback should always be chosen automatically as the "safe" default in every case
Forward fixes only apply to data rollbacks, never code rollbacks
questions.explain: The choice depends on which path gets to a correct state sooner, not on rollback being automatically safer.

questions.q: What is the key distinction this lesson draws between the two things commonly called "rollback"?
options: Code rollback (reverting and redeploying) versus data rollback (undoing the effects of already-written, already-displayed data)
There is no real distinction — both terms mean exactly the same thing
Code rollback only applies to KQL, data rollback only applies to Delta
Data rollback is always faster and easier than code rollback
questions.explain: One is mechanically simple thanks to existing CI/CD and Git machinery; the other is genuinely harder and sometimes impossible.
